facts.icd10_text: Age-related osteoporosis with current pathological fracture, vertebra(e), initial encounter

statements.text: Back pain began 07/18/2026 after bending to pick up a grandchild, 7 weeks before this visit.
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/02/2026: acute osteoporotic L1 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.
Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture.
Pain NRS 5/10 despite 6 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification.
Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture.
Interval increase in L1 vertebral body height loss compared with radiographs from 07/22/2026.
Focal kyphotic deformity at L1 measuring 28 degrees.
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program.
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/02/2026
Patient: Yon Cassin, 71-year-old female

MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/02/2026: acute osteoporotic L1 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging. Interval increase in L1 vertebral body height loss compared with radiographs from 07/22/2026. Focal kyphotic deformity at L1 measuring 28 degrees.

Impression:
Acute osteoporotic compression fracture of the L1 vertebral body with bone marrow edema. There is an interval increase in vertebral body height loss compared with prior imaging. A focal kyphotic deformity at L1 measuring 28 degrees is present.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/04/2026
Patient: Yon Cassin, 71-year-old female

History:
Back pain began 07/18/2026 after bending to pick up a grandchild, 7 weeks before this visit. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Pain NRS 5/10 despite 6 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture.

Clinical Findings:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Plan:
